newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices steady-off $1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices steady-off $1 - dealers.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hogs early Thursday sold steady to $1.00 per cwt lower as ample supplies continued to weigh on prices, livestock dealers said.
Rainfall overnight and early Thursday in the western Corn Belt allowed time for extra hog marketings as producers were forced from working in the fields, sources said.
Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold steady to $1.00 lower, with $53.50 to $54.00 paid in the country and $54.00 to $54.50 at plants, with an extreme top expected near $56.00 for top quality hogs.
Illinois hog prices were steady to $1.00 lower, at $52.50 to $54.50 in the country, with the latter called a scratch top, and $54.00 to $54.50 at plants.
Indiana/Ohio hogs sold $0.50 to $1.00 lower at $52.50 to $53.50 in the country and $54.00 to $54.50 at plants.
Pork prices were pressured as the increased hog supply this week plugged supply pipelines with fresh pork.
But lower pork values also were sparking increased sales which could lend support back to cash hog prices if the demand continues, sources said.
USDA in its carlot pork report reported 154.78 pork loads and 25.5 loads of trimmings sold Wednesday.
